title: 環境化学
subtitle: Environmental Chemistry
keywords: Global environment 2.Geochemical cycle of matter 3.Aquatic environments 4.Chemistry of water 5.Acid and base equilibria
educationalGoal: Environmental chemistry deals with chemical reactions on the cyclical changes and behavior of matter in the environment. You will learn the chemical reactions related to the behavior of matter and energy in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere to understand the ecosystem of the hydrosphere. The goal is to gain an understanding of the limnological environment from published data and to contribute to the conservation of the aquatic environment.
advice: 1. Structure of the earth, global energy balance, and greenhouse effect. 2. Cycles of matter, such as the carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorous cycle in the environment. 3. Introduction to the aquatic environment and water cycle. 4. Chemistry of water. 5. Acidity of environmental water and acid rain issues. 6. Oxidation and reduction in limnological environments. 7. Effect of dissolution of substances on water quality.
books: Textbooks: Limnological Environmental Chemistry (Kaoru Fujinaga, et al., Kyoritsu Shuppan Co., Ltd.) Reference Books: Aquatic Chemistry (Alan. G. Howard translated by M. Okumura, et al.) Reserved Books in the Library: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: A knowledge of high school level chemistry and biology is required to understand the lectures.

activityGoals.body: Comprehend the meaning of technical terms.
Explain the carbon and nitrogen cycles.
Understand the relation between the water and energy cycles.
Describe the effect of water characteristics on the global environment.
Explain the effect of acidity on environmental water.
Explain the seasonal variation in the water quality of a lake.

achievementLevels.ideal: Has an understanding of: ・ Technical terms in environmental chemistry ・ The carbon and nitrogen cycles in the environment ・ Effects of water acidity ・ Relation between rainwater pH and acid rain ・ Oxidation and reduction in terrestrial waters Must also be able to understand newspaper articles about chemical species and to distinguish between scientific accuracy and bias.
achievementLevels.standard: Using references, such as textbooks and dictionaries, can explain: ・ Technical terms in environmental chemistry ・ Cycles of matter in the environment, such as the carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles ・ Effects of water acidity ・ Relation between rainwater pH and acid rain ・ Oxidation and reduction in terrestrial waters ・ Relation between dissolution equilibrium and terrestrial water quality

lessons.content: What is environmental chemistry? Understanding solution concentration units.
lessons.assignments: Read the syllabus and check technical terms that you do not understand. Review the calculation of molar concentration of solutions in chapter 1 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Understanding the relationship between the energy balance of solar radiation and earth emissions in the global environment, and the structure of the earth.
Understanding the relationship between the energy balance of solar radiation, earth emissions, and the greenhouse effect.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 2 in the textbook. Calculate the maximum wavelength of radiation using Wien's radiation law.

lessons.content: Understanding the global nitrogen and carbon cycles in the environment.
lessons.assignments: Review chapters 1 and 2 in the textbook. Study for the 1st short test.

lessons.content: Understanding the global water cycle. 1st short test.
lessons.assignments: Review chapters 1 and 2 in the textbook.

lessons.content: Understanding the chemical properties of water.
Understanding the chemical properties of water on the terrestrial environment.
Understanding the concepts of acid-base equilibria, pH, and buffer action in solutions.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 4 in the textbook and calculate the pH of solutions. Study for the 2nd short test.

lessons.content: Understanding the effect of pH of rainwater on the aquatic environment and the acid rain problem. 2nd short test.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 4 in the textbook and calculate the pH of buffer solutions.

lessons.content: Understanding the effect of photosynthesis and decomposition of phytoplankton on the pH of lake water.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 4 in the textbook and calculate pH.

lessons.content: Understanding the concept of oxidation-reduction equilibria and the relationship between redox potential and eutrophication of lakes.
lessons.assignments: Review Nernst equation in chapter 6 of the textbook.

lessons.content: Understanding the concept of the E-pH stability diagram and the effect of redox potential on the dissolution of iron.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 6 in the textbook. Study for 3rd short test.

lessons.content: Understanding the concept of dissolution equilibria and dissolved substances in environmental water 3rd short test.
lessons.assignments: Calculate the solubility of dissolved substance in environmental water, and review chapter 5 in the textbook.

lessons.content: Understanding the relationship between the solubility of precipitates and the water quality of inland lake water.
lessons.assignments: Review chapter 5 in the textbook and calculate the solubility of dissolved substances in environmental water. Study for final exam.
